evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.85, LOWER-RIGHT reaction arrow: the drawn products are 'C3H6 + CH3OH2+' with '60%' printed underneath. NET REACTION ENCODED: protonated methyl isopropyl ether -> propene + protonated methanol, i.e. a 1,2-elimination in which the oxygen of the departing methanol takes the proton. MECHANISM (3 moves): <1> the C2-H7 sigma pair becomes the C1=C2 pi bond of propene; <2> the C1-O4 sigma pair drops onto the oxygen; <3> an oxygen lone pair captures the proton H7, giving CH3OH2+ (m/z 33.0335, curator-computed monoisotopic). The migrating hydrogen is written as an isotope-tagged explicit atom [1H:7] and the proton already on the oxygen as [1H:6], so both can carry atom maps. Book draws 0 arc(s): Equation 8.85 contains NO curved electron-pushing arrows at all - it is drawn with straight reaction/equilibrium arrows plus dashed 'partial bond' strokes that denote the loose bonds of the ion-neutral complexes. All three encoded moves are reconstructed for electron balance (not drawn on the page). DRAWN INTERMEDIATES DISCLOSED: the page reaches these products through TWO explicitly drawn non-covalent complexes that are not encoded as discrete species because partial bonds have no RDKit bond order - (i) the ion-neutral complex 'CH2(H)-CH(CH3)...O(+)(H)CH3' (dashed C...O, the labile methyl H drawn out), and (ii) the proton-bound complex '[CH2=CH-CH3 ... H(+) ... O(H)CH3]' in which the transferring proton is drawn between propene and methanol on two dotted lines with the '+' on that bridging H. The p.200 text explains the 60:40 split by the proton affinities PA(C3H6, CH3OH) = 7.8, 7.9 eV, i.e. the bridging proton is shared and the more basic partner keeps it. CONTEXT: the p.199 text introduces Equation 8.85 with 'In the absence of activating functional groups in EE ions, proton-exchange reactions can proceed in ion-molecule complexes (Equations 8.14, 8.85; Terlouw et al. 1986; Bowen 1991); demonstration of such pathways usually requires D-labeling. Here both the hydrogen lability and site receptivity' [continues on p.200] 'are determined by the relative proton affinities of the donor and acceptor sites: PA(C3H6, CH3OH) = 7.8, 7.9 eV. Note that the competitive dissociations of such a proton-bound isomer of (AB + H)+ produce AH+ and BH+, whose mass sum equals AB + 2.' The reacting ion is therefore the protonated molecule (AB+H)+ of methyl isopropyl ether, C4H11O+, curator-computed monoisotopic m/z 75.0804; the page prints no m/z for it. The two percentages printed on the page (40%, 60%) are the BRANCHING abundances of the two competing dissociation channels, not 70 eV EI relative intensities.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.85, so no MØD rule is cross-linked. Candidates checked and REJECTED: IMS_8_10 ('[C]1([H]2)([H]3)([H]4)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)[O+]8{=}[C]9([H]10)([H]11)>>...[C+]5....[O]8{=}[C]9...') and IMS_8_12 both require an OXOCARBENIUM precursor - the left side pins a DOUBLE bond [O+]8{=}[C]9 - whereas Equation 8.85 starts from a protonated ether whose O+ carries three single bonds (C, H, CH3); the pattern cannot match this substrate even though the bond that breaks (C-O, heterolytic, charge retained on carbon) is of the same inductive type. IMS_8_14_1/_1b (the proton-bound-complex rH pair) are additionally atom-unbalanced (their product half carries an extra methyl copy-pasted from IMS_8_13). The IMS_8_7_* 'hydrogen exchange in an ion-molecule complex' family operates on odd-electron ketone/enol systems, not on a protonated ether. Equation 8.85 is unmodelled by the current rule set.

The page prints '60%' under 'C3H6 + CH3OH2+': the printed branching abundance of this channel against the 40% channel of Equation 8.85a, NOT a 70 eV EI relative intensity. relative_intensity 0.6 stores the printed percentage; observed_mz 33.0335 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of CH3OH2+ (CH5O+, electron-mass corrected) - the page prints no m/z.

ms_context.activation_method: unspecified - the page names no ionization or activation experiment; the reacting ion is the protonated molecule (AB+H)+ of methyl isopropyl ether discussed in the p.199/200 text (Terlouw et al. 1986; Bowen 1991). ionization_method 'CI' is the curator's inference for how an (AB+H)+ ion is made, NOT a statement printed on the page
